correctness.rationale: Polar Fock diagonalization is exact. The adjacent-eigenvalue difference is a four-term exponential polynomial with at most three real zeros and strict endpoint signs. A differentiated uniform gamma-density expansion gives the even leading Gaussian mixture and odd cubic correction; three simple crossings for fixed delta>1 yield globally exactly two modal plateaus, whereas delta<1 yields one. The odd correction equals G(r)r(r^2-delta^2-3)/6 at the right peak, implying the explicit positive inner-minus-outer \(T^{-1}\) coefficient. The proof accounts for integer rounding with O(T^-3/2) in eigenvalue height. The 144 finite numerical assertions are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Two disconnected concentric localization windows make mode competition natural. The exact count of maximal Hermite degrees and the strict, parameter-explicit \(T^{-1}\) inward preference resolve a physical spectral-selection ambiguity that persists after a leading Gaussian approximation. The nontrivial exponential-polynomial zero bound turns local asymptotics into a complete global modal classification. The result is self-contained for the infinite fixed-delta family, and is not a trivial numeric slice or a restatement of an existing theorem.
